summary: State fire tower on Vulcan Hill, Dickinson County, reported under construction in May 1939; a 1984 survey note calls it abandoned. No source read says what remains.

facts.status_note: Called abandoned in a 1984 survey note; no source read says whether any of the tower still stands
facts.agency: State Department of Conservation (1939 newspaper says 'the conservation department')

access.note: The hill was owned by the Brair Mountain ski resort in 1984; no later access source read

events.note: Erection under way per the Ironwood Daily Globe, 25 May 1939; completion not confirmed by a second source
The 1984 National Geodetic Survey recovery note calls the tower abandoned; the year it was abandoned is not given

evidence.supports: erection: state conservation department erecting a new fire tower on Vulcan Hill, May 1939
evidence.quote: In order to provide additional fire protection in this part of the district the conservation department is erecting a new fire tower on Vulcan Hill.
Workmen are now preparing the base and lower part of the tower, which will be 125 feet high.

evidence.supports: straight-ladder type; in use about two weeks after the report
evidence.quote: The tower, one of the straight ladder type, will be in use in about two weeks.
Dickinson County - State Department of Conservation

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: 125 ft is the 1939 planned height from a newspaper item quoted secondhand; 149 ft comes from a personal collector's site and is not checked. The 1939 event is recorded as 'other' (erection under way), not 'built': the May 1939 report says the tower would be in use in about two weeks, and no completion source was read. Search results mentioned a 1934 date for a Vulcan tower on another compilation page; not read, so not used. Brair spelling follows the 1984 NGS note. Ski-area history from search results (Norway Mountain, closures, reopening) was not read and is not used. Record status 'unknown' is left as is; the 1984 note supports 'abandoned' only as of 1984.
